graph_warnings: Do NOT: increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012)  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 11 and 12.1]

Underfill: Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor.  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 11 and 12.1]
LOTO (SAF-003): Any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or reaching into the machine  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.2]
LOTO (SAF-003): Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.2]
Machine Safety Rules: Never clear a jam while the machine is running, never reach past a guard, and never bypass or tape over a guard switch  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 6.3 and 6.4]
Machine Safety Rules: Never use compressed air near open bottles or broken glass  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 6.3 and 6.4]

Fill Time Setting: The fill time must NOT be changed by operators. Changing it needs written approval from engineering. A longer fill time does not fix underfill: it hides the real cause and makes bottles overflow.  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 10]
Escalate to Maintenance Supervisor: Do not attempt electrical repairs. Always call maintenance.  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 13]

For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings.  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
Fill Valve Seal Replacement: Only food-grade lubricant FGL-1. Any other lubricant contaminates the product.  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
First-Bottle Check is MANDATORY — normal production must not restart without it  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 10 and Section 11]
Sanitation Rinse is MANDATORY — never skip it after a seal change: the first bottles would carry lubricant into the product  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 9, FL-101-SOP Sections 4, 9, 12.3 and 17]
Fill Valve Seal Replacement sign-off: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check before normal production restarts.  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
Do NOT: raise the fill time to fix underfill

FILL VALVE SEAL REPLACEMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PURPOSE

This work instruction explains how to replace the seal kit in an FL-101
fill valve. A worn seal is the most common cause of underfill alarms.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

Record what you found. If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same
time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too
long.

10. TROUBLESHOOTING AFTER THE JOB

  What you see                        Check                     Action
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Valve still drips                   Seal seated correctly?    Refit the seal
  Valve still underfills, no drip     Nozzle blocked?           Clean the nozzle
  All valves underfill                Supply pressure?          SOP Section 12.4
  Overfill for 2 to 3 minutes only    Normal settling           No action
  Overfill after 5 minutes            Valve fully clicked in?   Refit the valve
  Leak at the valve body              O-ring missing?           Fit a new O-ring

11. SIGN-OFF

11. SIGN-OFF

  - The shift supervisor must sign off the first-bottle check before normal
    production restarts.
  - Record in the maintenance log: date, valve numbers changed, seal kits
    used, condition of the old seals, first-bottle check results, and
    your name.

12. REVISION HISTORY

6. SAFETY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

6.1 PPE required on Filling Line 1
  - Safety glasses at all times
  - Cut-resistant gloves when handling glass or change parts
  - Hearing protection
  - Safety shoes

Record every check on the pre-start checklist. The shift lead signs it.

8.1 Fill valves and seals
  - Look at each of the 24 fill valves for cracks or dripping.
  - A valve that drips between fills has a worn seal. Report it before
    starting.
  - Seal kits (part SEAL-FV-24) are replaced every 3 months or every
    1,500 running hours, whichever comes first.
  - Spare seal kits are kept in the Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2.
    The minimum stock is 10 kits.

8.2 Infeed and guide rails
  - Check the guide rails are set for the bottle size being run:
      500 ml bottles: rail position A
      330 ml bottles: rail position B
  - Check the rails are locked and the matching star wheel is fitted.

8.3 Product supply
  - Check the bowl level indicator shows NORMAL.
  - Check the product supply pressure is 1.5 to 2.0 bar.
  - The supply filter (part FLT-PS-10) is cleaned once a week. Check the
    date on the filter tag.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone
           is in danger).
  Step 2 — Read the checkweigher report. It shows which valve numbers are
           underfilling.
  Step 3 — Look at those valves. Dripping means a worn seal: call the
           maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using work
           instruction WI-FL101-001.
  Step 4 — No dripping: lock out the machine (Section 6.2) and clean the
           nozzle of that valve.
  Step 5 — Check the product supply pressure (Section 12.4).

Do NOT increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn
seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012).

Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually
several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and
call the maintenance supervisor.

12.2 Infeed Jam
Alarm message: "Infeed jam — bottles stopped at infeed"

10. OPERATING SETTINGS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  Bottle:                  500 ml glass (or 330 ml after a changeover)
  Target fill:             500 ml
  Allowed fill range:      495 to 505 ml (checkweigher rejects outside this)
  Line speed:              120 bottles per minute (maximum 130)
  Product supply pressure: 1.5 to 2.0 bar
  Low pressure alarm:      below 1.3 bar
  Fill time:               3.2 seconds, factory set

The fill time must NOT be changed by operators. Changing it needs written
approval from engineering. A longer fill time does not fix underfill: it
hides the real cause and makes bottles overflow (see NCR-2026-012).

1. WHAT HAPPENED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

On the night shift of 16 January 2026, FL-101 raised underfill alarms
three times: at 21:40, 23:55 and 02:10.

After each alarm the operator increased the fill time to push more water
into the bottles: first from 3.2 to 3.6 seconds, then to 3.9 seconds.

The longer fill time made most valves overflow. Water spilled onto the
bottles and the conveyor, labels were damaged at the labeller, and the
line stopped twice to clean up spillage.

21:40  First underfill alarm. Line stopped 15 minutes. Operator raised
         fill time 3.2 to 3.6 s and restarted.
  21:55  Underfill stopped. Overflow started on most valves.
  23:10  Line stopped 25 minutes to clean spillage from the conveyor.
  23:55  Second underfill alarm. Line stopped 15 minutes. Operator raised
         fill time to 3.9 s.
  01:20  Labeller reported wet, peeling labels. Line stopped 40 minutes.
  02:10  Third underfill alarm. Line stopped. Shift supervisor called.
  02:25  Supervisor found valves 7, 12, 13 and 19 dripping.
  02:45  No spare seal kits in the cabinet. Line stood down until morning.
         (Stops before this point: 15 + 25 + 15 + 40 + 35 minutes = 2 hours
         10 minutes.)
  06:30  Maintenance fitted seal kits from the main store. Fill time
         restored to 3.2 s.
  07:35  Rinse and first-bottle check passed. Line restarted.

  - Underfill is a seal problem until proven otherwise. Check for dripping
